subject: Fiscal Year 2016 Property Tax Classification
overview: The City Council conducted its annual tax classification hearing, approving the minimum residential factor to shift the tax burden while rejecting residential, small commercial, and open space exemptions, as well as a proposed $1 million tax levy reduction. The Council also approved a $250,000 transfer for state-mandated property revaluation and debated school department staffing and council decorum.

items.title: Citizen Petition on Owner-Occupied Residential Tax Exemption
items.summary: Andrew Castagnetti petitioned the Council to adopt a 20 percent owner-occupied residential tax exemption under state law, after which the Council voted to attach public testimony on the matter to the tax classification hearing.

items.title: Fiscal Year 2016 Property Tax Allocation and Classification
items.summary: Following extensive debate over property valuations, reserves, and commercial impacts, the Council approved the minimum residential factor of 0.897446 and voted against an open space discount, a residential exemption, and a small commercial exemption.

items.title: Resolution to Reduce Proposed Tax Levy by $1 Million
items.summary: Vice President Lungo-Koehn offered a resolution requesting that the administration reduce the proposed property tax levy by $1 million using available free cash reserves, but the motion failed on a roll call vote.

items.title: Committee Report on Fiscal Year 2016 Tax Rate
items.summary: The Council approved the Committee of the Whole report from December 1, 2015, regarding the fiscal year 2016 tax rate.

items.title: Overlay Surplus Transfer for Triennial Revaluation
items.summary: Approved a request from the mayor to transfer $250,000 from the overlay surplus account to fund the state-mandated triennial property revaluation.

items.title: Committee Report on $300,000 Bond Request
items.summary: The Council accepted a committee report regarding a $300,000 bond request and voted to table the matter.

items.title: Tabled Resolutions on Tufts EMS and Resident Permit Parking
items.summary: Resolutions requesting a meeting regarding Tufts Emergency Medical Services and an update from the Traffic Commission on resident permit parking were both tabled.

items.title: Water Conservation in Municipal Buildings
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a report from the Office of Energy and Environment regarding past and planned water conservation measures within city-owned buildings.

items.title: Discussion on Freedom of Speech and Council Decorum
items.summary: Councilor Penta initiated a discussion regarding free speech rights at the podium and during meetings, prompting debate over council etiquette and political comments.

items.title: School Department Staffing, Wages, and Public Relations Position
items.summary: The Council approved an amended resolution requesting that the superintendent report back on wage increases for cafeteria workers and kindergarten aides, as well as the job description and funding source for a newly created school public relations position.

items.title: Commendations and Condolences
items.summary: The Council approved a citation for Henry and Evelyn Miller for work with the disability community, commended veteran Jimmy Granara upon completing his service, and held a moment of silence in memory of former Medford Daily Mercury editor Alfonso "Al" Fresa.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The records of the meeting of December 1, 2015, were approved.
